title: Local perfectness and invertibility of the strict tower projection
statement: Fix small ringed tensor corners A and B, an edge e with isomorphic structural ring map and exact additive module pullback, normalized coefficient reductions rA and rB for strict augmented sequences QA and QB of complexes, and a normalized pullback comparison p:PullReduction e rA rB [def-sbc-strict-augmented-coefficient-presentation]. If every derived coefficient QA(n) is locally perfect [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], then every QB(n) is locally perfect. For every normalized pair of total derived strict inverse limits, normalized total derived direct image d and normalized tower adjunction a, and every unbounded derived object E on B, the adjunct projection e a p E is an isomorphism in the derived category of strict module towers [def-sbc-strict-coefficient-exchange-arrows]. No common bounds or ranks for the coefficients, and no completeness of E, are assumed.

source.place: Tags 0944, 0E48 and 0A07; explicit strict augmented-complex refinement by E3

proof.text: Pull back a covering on which a level coefficient is a bounded finite-free-retract complex. The strict perfect pullback theorem carries its degreewise splitting to the target with unchanged ranks. Exact inverse image carries the quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism. Pullbacks of the covering epimorphism cover, so this proves local perfectness of QB(n) through the given coefficient isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the normalized tower evaluation theorem and the representative equation for p.pull to evaluate the defining transpose of projection e a p E. Its transpose is the usual derived tensor pullback comparison followed by the ambient counit tensored with the coefficient. Thus the evaluated morphism is exactly the perfect coefficient projection map, which is invertible by the ringed-site perfect projection theorem.

proof.text: Exact evaluation computes each homology object of a strict tower levelwise. For the cone of the projection all evaluated homology objects vanish, so every homology tower is zero and its cone is acyclic. Consequently the projection is invertible in the localization. This detects isomorphisms only, not equality of arrows.

theorem strictPerfectTowerProjection
    (he : IsIso e.ringMap) (p : PullReduction e rA rB)
    (hperfect : ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ, IsPerfectOnRingedSiteOfUniverses.{u, u, 0, w}
      A.ring (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (QA.obj n))) :
    (∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ, IsPerfectOnRingedSiteOfUniverses.{u, u, 0, w}
      B.ring (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (QB.obj n))) ∧
    ∀ (lA : StrictProjectionLimit A) (lB : StrictProjectionLimit B)
      (d : StrictProjectionDirectImage e lB lA) (a : TowerAdjunction e d)
      (E : B.mateDerived), IsIso (projection e a p E)
